title: Saxophone harmonization and influences: Hickman, Gifford, Challis
summary: Carter recalls Art Hickman, Gene Gifford and Bill Challis as arranger models.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: This leads me to another point, I mean, about the saxophone chorus, and Gunther Dr. Schuller, in his book, I just want to see if in your recollection this is correct -- mentions that a lot of what he calls early stock arrangements featured three part saxophone harmonizations.
Now what bands, for example, might you have been listening to which -- with regard to writing saxophone choruses and so forth -- does the name Art Hickman ring any bell at all?
Yes, it does -- but nothing that I listening to. No. remember him doing.
Now Because he has been claimed and various want to people often claim that this was one of the earliest bands to use a fuller saxophone section.
Oh, really? I wasn't aware of that.

What about a few other arrangers we can mention -- certainly Don Redman was a very important figure, but what about some of the white bands and some of the white arrangers for the Goldkette Gold-Keg band, for example?
Well, I think that the only one I -- the only two I remember, Gene Gifford and outstandingly, I might say, Bill Challis.
Uh huh. Now just in general, how could you describe their style in general? Or something

Gene Gifford. I think Gene Gifford did a thing called 'White Heat' -- would that sound right? 'White Heat' for the Goldkette band. A couple of things he did were kind of ... his arrangements, if I remember, I would feel that Gene Gifford might have been influenced somewhat by John Nesbitt, who arranged for McKinney's Cotton Pickers.

Bill Challis at the time, his arrangements were quite different from Gene Gifford's. What he did, I liked much better, you know. Harmonically and stylewise. 'Cause I never was able to look at any of his music, but I heard it, you know.
Uh huh. Well, what about ... I'm sorry?

I might correct myself on that, because I may have seen some of his music, because I understand that he wrote arrangements for Fletcher Henderson, but what arrangements I played in Henderson's band that were written by Challis I can't recall any titles now.
So I must've played some of his arrangements.
